## Context / Problem

Evaluating a Pass-1 change on Sonnet when production runs Opus (or vice versa) confounds the measurement: prior work showed Sonnet degrades past ~3 criteria per turn while Opus is flat, so a delta could be the model, not the change. Two further hazards: the production model classes (`rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]`: frontier = `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, standard = `bedrock:…claude-sonnet-4-6`) carry an Anthropic-direct fallback, and `_intersect_capabilities` (`src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py`) collapses a mixed chain's `prompt_cache_style` to `none` whenever the chain's candidates disagree — which is why cache reads dropped to zero on 2026-08-12 and review cost roughly doubled. An eval run that carries the production Anthropic-direct fallback alongside a Bedrock primary is STILL a mixed chain to `_intersect_capabilities`, even though the primary is Bedrock — so checking only the primary is not sufficient to guarantee caching survives.

## Approach

Build `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/parity.py` as a standalone module in THIS ticket (`tier1.py`, `tier2.py`, and `report.py` do not exist yet — they are built by later tickets in this epic, `presolar-finable-binturong`/Tier-1, `peaceable-choppy-sapsucker`/Tier-2, and the report module bundled with the Tier-0 ticket `bouncy-peacockish-titmouse`; THIS ticket only builds and unit-tests `parity.py`'s functions in isolation, exposing the API those later tickets will import and call — it does not itself edit tier1.py/tier2.py/report.py, which are out of scope here):

- **Pinned targets, with an ACTUALLY homogeneous chain (not just a primary check)**: `resolve_pinned_model(pass_name)` maps `pass_name` to a production model class via a fixed constant `PASS_MODEL_CLASS = {"pass1": "frontier", "pass2": "standard"}` (Pass 1 = finders = frontier/Opus, Pass 2 = verifier = standard/Sonnet; Pass 3/decide is deterministic and never resolves a model, so it is not in this map — calling with an unmapped `pass_name` raises `ValueError`). It reuses the existing model-class resolution seam: `rebar.llm.model_classes.load_class_slots()` for the resolved slots, `resolve_class(name, slots)` for the class's primary `provider:model` string, requiring that primary to start with `bedrock:` (refusing/raising otherwise). It returns a SINGLE model id string — the primary only — and explicitly does NOT return or expose the class's `fallback` list (`resolve_fallback_chain` is not called by this function at all; the homogeneous-chain guarantee comes from the eval caller NEVER constructing a fallback list in the first place, not from filtering an existing one). Every eval-run caller (later Tier-1/Tier-2 tickets) MUST build its `LLMConfig`/model resolution with this single pinned id and no `fallback_targets` — that is the actual mechanism that keeps `_intersect_capabilities` from ever seeing a second, Anthropic candidate to intersect against, so `prompt_cache_style` is never collapsed. `check_model_parity(pass_name, resolved_id, baseline_ran_model)` refuses when `resolved_id` differs from a supplied baseline `ran_model` for that pass, unless an explicit `allow_model_change=True` is passed, in which case the result is labelled `model-change` and callers must never diff it against a baseline with a different id.
- **Result stamping helper**: `stamp_pass_model(result, pass_name, model_id)` and `refuse_diff_on_model_mismatch(result_a, result_b)` — the latter raises when two result dicts carry different per-pass model ids under a `models: {pass: model_id}` key. (Later tickets call this from `report.py`, which does not exist yet.)
- **Caching check**: `check_cache_effective(usage_rows)` asserts from a list of usage-log row dicts that `cache_read_tokens > 0` on at least one row after the first, returning a `{"cached": bool, "first_cache_hit_row": int | None}` verdict callers can fold into a report or the ledger. (Later tickets call this after a live run and fold the verdict into the report/ledger — those integrations don't exist yet.)
- No production config is changed by this ticket; the homogeneous chain is composed in-process, in this module only, by never introducing a fallback to the eval run's model resolution.

**Corpus field addition needed by this ticket's own tests and by later parity checks**: `corpus.py`'s `_build_sidecar_row` (`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py`) currently emits a row with `verdict`/`material_fingerprint`/etc. but does not surface `provider_provenance.ran_model` from the sidecar's `data` dict. Add a `ran_model` key to the emitted row (`data.get("provider_provenance", {}).get("ran_model")`, `None` when absent). This is additive to the row SHAPE but IS a material content change: `_compute_manifest` hashes every key of every row, so adding `ran_model` changes `content_hash` for every future corpus build — the already-committed `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/corpus-2026-08-29.manifest.json` becomes stale and must be regenerated and re-committed as part of this ticket's own integration step.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/parity.py` (new)
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py` (edit: add `ran_model` to the sidecar row)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/corpus-<date>.manifest.json` (regenerated: new content_hash from the added row field)
- `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_parity.py` (new)

## Testing

Unit: `resolve_pinned_model("pass1")` and `("pass2")` resolve the frontier/standard Bedrock ids as a bare string (never a list/chain); an unmapped pass_name raises `ValueError`; a config whose frontier class resolves to a non-Bedrock primary is refused; `resolve_pinned_model`'s return value is asserted to carry no fallback structure (a plain `str`, not a dict/list a caller could misuse to smuggle a fallback back in) even when the underlying class config DOES have a configured `fallback` (proving the fallback is dropped, not merely unread). `refuse_diff_on_model_mismatch` raises on differing per-pass model ids and accepts identical ones; `check_cache_effective` marks a usage-log fixture with zero cache reads as uncached and one with `cache_read_tokens > 0` on a later row as cached. A corpus row built from a sidecar carrying `provider_provenance.ran_model` surfaces it as `ran_model`; one without the key surfaces `ran_model: None`. Live check (cache effectiveness against a real run) happens as part of the Tier-1 reproduction run in a later ticket, not here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `resolve_pinned_model` maps `pass1`/`pass2` to the frontier/standard Bedrock ids as a bare string with no fallback structure returned, even when the class has a configured fallback, and refuses a resolved primary that is not a Bedrock id; checked by unit tests.
- [ ] `refuse_diff_on_model_mismatch` raises when two result dicts carry differing per-pass model ids and accepts identical ones; checked by a unit test.
- [ ] `check_cache_effective` correctly classifies a cached vs. an uncached usage-row fixture; checked by a unit test.
- [ ] `corpus.py`'s sidecar row surfaces `ran_model` from `provider_provenance.ran_model`, absent-safe; the corpus manifest is regenerated so its `content_hash` reflects the new field; checked by a unit test and by re-running the corpus build.
- [ ] Unit tests pass in `make test`.
- [ ] No LLM calls; checked by running with no provider credentials.
